title: Monopoly & Imperfect Competition (HL) Adventure 3: Kinked Demand & Contestable Markets
welcome_lead: Today you'll bend the demand curve with Sweezy and contest the market with Baumol.
meta_desc: Economics HL: kinked demand model (Sweezy 1939) and contestable markets (Baumol 1982).
final_note: You explained the kinked demand model and the contestable markets theory.

concepts.def: Free entry & exit; sunk cost low

walkthroughs.body_html:
Paul Sweezy (1939) explained sticky oligopoly prices.

If a firm raises price, rivals don't follow — demand is elastic, sales collapse.

If a firm cuts price, rivals follow to retain share — demand is inelastic, gains small.

Result: a kink at current price. MR has a vertical jump, so cost shifts in that range leave price unchanged.

William Baumol (1982): even a single seller behaves competitively if entry and exit are free and sunk costs are low.

Threat of hit-and-run entry forces the incumbent to keep price near average cost.

Implication: regulators should police entry barriers, not just count firms.

The kinked demand model explains price stickiness; Baumol explains moderation by potential rivals.

Together they show that oligopolies can be more or less competitive depending on rivalry intensity and entry barriers — and that policy should focus on contestability.
